headline: Sterling is about 1.349 dollars on Thursday morning, near its highest since mid September, as the dollar stays soft after the midterms and oil has dropped below $100 a barrel (about £74). The Bank of England decides at 16:00 Dubai today, where a rise to 4% is expected, and the US jobs figures follow on Friday 6 November.

drivers.title: The midterms
drivers.text: Democrats won both houses of Congress, which markets read as gridlock in Washington and a lower chance of renewed strikes on Iran. The dollar index fell 0.36% on 4 November and was about 101.41 in Asian trade on 5 November, while US ten year yields closed at 4.89%, down about 8 basis points.

drivers.title: The Fed
drivers.text: Markets price about an 81% chance of a Fed rise in December, up from about 77%, according to the CME FedWatch tool as reported by Reuters on 5 November, after private payrolls (ADP) rose 86,000 in October against 69,000 expected. Dallas Fed President Logan has said the Fed needs at least two more quarter point rises, which keeps support under the dollar.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: Bank Rate is 3.75%, and a rise to 4% is expected at 16:00 Dubai on 5 November, the first rise since August 2023, with a vote of seven to two forecast. Markets also price at least three more quarter point rises next year, so the Bank's guidance and the vote split will count for more than the rise itself.

drivers.title: Oil and Iran
drivers.text: Brent settled at $94.62 a barrel (about £70) on 4 November, down 8.7% on the day and more than 14% this week, as US and Iranian officials signal openness to a settlement and a Democratic Congress may curb war funding. Analysts warn the risk of escalation remains, and renewed fighting would tend to lift oil and the dollar.

lower: A breakdown in the Iran talks or renewed US strikes that send oil back above $100 (about £74), which would tend to lift the dollar as a safe haven.
Low US jobless claims today, below the forecast of 197,000, or a jobs number above 65,000 on 6 November, which would firm up a December Fed rise and lift the dollar.
A Bank of England that raises rates today but signals no more to come, or more members voting against the rise than the two expected, which would take away support the pound already has.
higher: Further progress in the Iran talks that keeps oil falling, which would tend to weaken the dollar.
A Bank of England that raises rates today and points to more rises, or a vote with fewer members against, which would lift the pound.
Weak US jobs figures on 6 November, with payrolls below 65,000 or unemployment above 4.2%, which would make a December Fed rise less certain and weaken the dollar.
Further falls in US yields as markets digest a Democratic Congress, narrowing the gap with UK rates.
watch: The Bank of England decides at 16:00 Dubai today, Thursday 5 November, where a rise to 4% on a vote of seven to two is expected, and the Governor speaks at 16:30 Dubai; a firmer message on further rises would help someone selling pounds for dirhams and a cautious one would hurt. US weekly jobless claims follow at 17:30 Dubai, forecast at 197,000, and the US jobs figures at 17:30 Dubai on Friday 6 November, forecast at 65,000; weaker figures would help and stronger ones would hurt.

feed.title: Oil has fallen below $100 after the midterms
feed.text: Brent crude fell 8.7% on Wednesday to settle at $94.62 a barrel (about £70), its first close below $100 since late August, and US crude fell 8.3% to $88.12 (about £65), taking the fall this week to more than 14%. Traders read the Democratic win in Congress, the Vice President's remark that the war cost the party the election, and the President's comment that he has no immediate plans to strike Iran as signs that the conflict may end sooner. Cheaper oil and less Gulf tension tend to weaken the dollar, and US ten year yields fell about 8 basis points to 4.89%.

feed.title: Sterling has edged higher as the dollar stays soft
feed.text: GBP/USD dipped to about 1.3455 at 20:45 Dubai on Wednesday evening, recovered to about 1.3475 by 21:30 Dubai and held between about 1.3460 and 1.3470 overnight, then rose from about 1.3477 at 04:00 Dubai to about 1.3490 by 07:15 Dubai. EUR/USD rose in step, from about 1.1233 to about 1.1257, so the move came mainly from a softer dollar, with the dollar index near 101.41 in Asian trade after falling 0.36% on Wednesday. Societe Generale also points to traders in the pound closing bets against it ahead of the Bank of England decision today.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed despite softer US services figures
feed.text: The US ISM services index came in at 54.5 against 54.8 expected and 54.9 in September, with new orders down to 55.9 from 59.8, but the prices index stayed high at 73.0 and the employment index rose to 51.4 from 50.1. A softer reading usually weakens the dollar, while stubborn prices keep a Fed rise in December in view, and the dollar kept the firmer tone it had found in the hour before: GBP/USD, already down from about 1.3486 at 18:35 Dubai to 1.3477 just before the release, dipped to about 1.3470 within a minute and slid to about 1.3463 by 19:20 Dubai. EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1265 at 18:30 Dubai to 1.1234, so the dollar has won back part of its overnight fall across the board; no report read names a single cause beyond the release.

feed.title: Sterling has touched 1.35 and slipped back
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3484 at 16:20 Dubai to about 1.3498 by 16:30 Dubai, its highest since mid September, then eased to about 1.3487 by 16:35 Dubai; EUR/USD rose and fell in step, from about 1.1255 to about 1.1267 and back to 1.1257, so the swing came from the dollar rather than from news about the pound. No report read names a fresh cause for it: the dollar index was about 0.4% lower on the day after the midterm result, with US ten year yields down about 6 basis points to about 4.91%, and the US ISM services index at 19:00 Dubai is the next scheduled figure.

feed.title: The dollar has steadied after its overnight fall
feed.text: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3493 at 14:25 Dubai to about 1.3476 by 14:45 Dubai and touched about 1.3469 at 15:05 Dubai, before recovering to about 1.3480 by 15:35 Dubai; EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1258 to a low of about 1.1234, so the move came from a slightly firmer dollar rather than from news about the pound. No report read names a single cause: euro area inflation came in as expected at 4% (core 2.5%) shortly before, giving the euro no fresh lift, and ING called the dollar's fall on the midterm result tentative, noting that a strong US economy and a Fed ready to raise rates still support it. The US ADP jobs and ISM services figures come out later today.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened as Democrats win Congress
feed.text: Democrats have won the Senate and, on the latest reports, the House, ending Republican control of Congress for the last two years of the President's term. Markets read a divided Washington as less room for new spending and borrowing, and US ten year yields fell about 4 basis points to 4.92%, so the dollar fell across the board: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3407 at 03:00 Dubai, as the early returns came in, to about 1.3471 by 05:30 Dubai, while EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1188 to 1.1258. Sterling has held the gain and was near 1.3484 at 12:30 Dubai, its highest since mid September.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed after more US job openings than expected
feed.text: US job openings rose to 7.52 million in September against about 7.1 million expected, up from a revised 7.19 million in August, a sign that demand for workers is holding up. A firm job market keeps a Fed rise in December in view and supports US yields, with the ten year yield near 4.95% and up on the day, so the dollar gained: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3431 at 19:00 Dubai to about 1.3423 within two minutes and to about 1.3410 by 19:30 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1196 to 1.1176. Hires and quits also rose, and sterling has since recovered to about 1.3424 at 22:10 Dubai.

feed.title: Americans are voting in the midterm elections
feed.text: Polls are open across the United States today and results will come through overnight into Wednesday in Dubai, so there is no result yet to measure. Pollsters and prediction markets make the Democrats favourites to win the House and the Senate, with prediction markets giving them about a 73% chance of the Senate as of Monday. A divided Congress would make large new spending or tax plans harder to pass, and a result different from what is priced could move the dollar overnight.

feed.title: The dollar has eased as oil slipped on Iran deal reports
feed.text: GBP/USD went from about 1.3412 at 14:40 Dubai to a low of about 1.3401 at 16:30 Dubai, then jumped from about 1.3414 to 1.3427 in the two minutes to 17:30 Dubai and was near 1.3423 at 18:40 Dubai; EUR/USD rose at the same moment from about 1.1182 to 1.1197, so the move came from a weaker dollar rather than from the pound. It came as oil slid, with WTI falling from $98.50 (about £73) around 16:30 Dubai to $94.05 (about £70) by 17:45 Dubai after President Trump told Fox News that US aid to Israel ends at the year end and an unconfirmed report said Washington had approved a draft agreement with Iran; cheaper oil and hopes of a deal tend to weaken the dollar. Iran's Mohsen Rezaei later called the US response unconvincing and oil recovered to about flat, while US ten year yields were about 4.93%, up on the day, ahead of the job openings figures at 19:00 Dubai and the midterm results overnight.

feed.title: Sterling is flat as oil climbs back towards $107
feed.text: GBP/USD has barely moved over four hours, from about 1.3415 at 10:35 Dubai to about 1.3412 at 14:35 Dubai, with a high of about 1.3426 at 12:10 Dubai and a low of about 1.3405 at 10:45 Dubai. Brent extended its rise after the reports of US strikes on Qeshm Island, reaching $106.61 (about £79) at 11:44 Dubai and nearly $107 (about £80) by 12:52 Dubai, while an Iranian official said peace negotiations were far from an agreement; dearer oil and Gulf tension tend to lift the dollar, and EUR/USD eased from about 1.1205 at 11:30 Dubai to about 1.1181 at 14:00 Dubai, which points to a slightly firmer dollar through the European morning. No UK figures were due today, and the market is waiting for the US midterm results, the Bank of England on Thursday and the US jobs figures on Friday.

feed.title: Sterling has edged back up as the dollar eased through the Asian morning
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from an overnight low of about 1.3397 at 07:15 Dubai to about 1.3415 by 09:35 Dubai and was still near 1.3415 at 10:35 Dubai, leaving aside one stray trade at 1.3478, while EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1182 to about 1.1193, which points to a slightly softer dollar rather than news about the pound. No report read names a cause for the drift: oil has held its small early rise after the reports of US strikes on Qeshm Island, and no further escalation has been reported. The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its rate to 4.85% this morning as expected, and the Australian dollar fell, so that decision did not weaken the dollar more widely.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed after reports of US strikes on Iran
feed.text: US officials told the Wall Street Journal and CBS News that American forces made limited defensive strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz, after Revolutionary Guard forces fired on a US aircraft, and Brent rose 0.5% to $105.25 (about £79) by 05:04 Dubai after falling 7.6% on Monday. Gulf tension tends to lift the dollar as a safe haven, and GBP/USD fell from about 1.3414 at 04:39 Dubai to about 1.3401 at 04:42 Dubai while EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1192 to 1.1184, which points to the dollar, though no report read gives the exact time the news broke. Sterling has since held near 1.3400, a little below Monday evening's 1.3409, with an overnight low of about 1.3395.

feed.title: Sterling is little changed as oil slumps and US shares fade
feed.text: Brent fell 7.7% to $104.66 (about £78) on hopes for US and Iran diplomacy, and an Iranian report at 22:25 Dubai said the two sides were close to a preliminary agreement, although neither government has confirmed it. Cheaper oil and easier tension tend to weaken the dollar, yet GBP/USD fell from about 1.3419 at 21:50 Dubai to about 1.3402 at 22:50 Dubai, and EUR/USD fell from about 1.1204 to about 1.1190, which points to a firmer dollar. No report read names a cause for that step, though it came as US technology shares turned lower on selling in chip stocks. GBP/USD then recovered to about 1.3409, little changed from about 1.3415 four hours earlier, with a high of about 1.3422 and a low of about 1.3402 over that time, leaving aside one stray trade at 1.3431.

feed.title: Sterling has edged lower after a stronger US factory survey
feed.text: The ISM manufacturing index for October came in at 55.5 against 54.5 expected and 54.5 last time, while its prices measure fell to 75.2 against about 77.5 expected. Stronger activity tends to support the dollar by keeping a December Fed rise in view, but softer price pressure limits that effect, and investingLive notes that some of the gain came from inventories and slower deliveries rather than new orders. GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3421 at 19:00 Dubai to 1.3416 within three minutes, returned to about 1.3423 by 19:10 Dubai and was about 1.3414 at 19:38 Dubai, a small move, and EUR/USD eased from about 1.1212 to about 1.1196, which points to the dollar.

feed.title: Sterling has recovered part of its slide as oil stayed lower
feed.text: West Texas crude was down about 4% near $99.80 (about £74) on hopes for a US and Iran deal, although no agreement has been confirmed, and cheaper oil and easier tension tend to weaken the dollar. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3402 at 15:00 Dubai to about 1.3425 at 17:38 Dubai, then eased to about 1.3418. The last step came between 17:36 and 17:38 Dubai, when EUR/USD also rose from about 1.1210 to about 1.1220, which points to the dollar, but no report read names a cause for that step, and the US factory survey is still to come at 19:00 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has given back its morning gain as the dollar steadied
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3444 at 13:15 Dubai to about 1.3405 at 14:40 Dubai, a drop of 0.29%, while EUR/USD fell 0.22% from about 1.1232 to about 1.1207, which points mainly to the dollar recovering, with the pound slightly the weaker. No report read names a cause for the slide. UK factory figures at 13:30 Dubai matched the first estimate at 52.8, so they were no surprise, and the fall had begun before them. Reuters notes the Bank of England rise to 4% on Thursday is widely expected and that the Bank may push back on the three to four further rises priced for 2027, which would weigh on the pound if it does.

feed.title: Sterling has touched 1.3444 on a weaker dollar, then given part of it back
feed.text: Investing.com says the dollar eased as oil fell 2% to 3% on reports that President Trump wants diplomacy with Iran to run its course, and that the pound's gain owes more to the dollar than to UK fundamentals. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3419 at 12:30 Dubai to about 1.3444 by 13:15 Dubai, and EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1197 to about 1.1232, which points to the dollar. GBP/USD then slipped back to about 1.3423 by 13:40 Dubai and EUR/USD to about 1.1216; no report read names a cause for that pullback.

feed.title: The dollar has slipped further as the mood improved before the midterms
feed.text: US stock futures rose between 0.4% and 0.9% and West Texas crude fell about 2%, after a weekend with no US strikes on Iran and talk of a shorter timetable for reopening Hormuz, though Washington has not accepted that plan. Better risk appetite reduces demand for the dollar as a safe haven, and ING says traders may also trim dollar positions before Tuesday's vote. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3395 at 10:30 Dubai to about 1.3416 at 11:35 Dubai and EUR/USD rose from 1.1175 to 1.1187, which points mainly to the dollar, with the pound slightly the stronger; no report read names a single event behind the step, and no UK figure had come out.

feed.title: The dollar has eased as oil fell further on hopes for Iran diplomacy
feed.text: Brent was down more than 3% at about $110 (about £82) at 07:55 Dubai, after Axios reported that President Trump told Israel's prime minister he wanted to give diplomacy more time before any further strikes. FXStreet says optimism about a breakthrough is weakening the dollar as a safe haven, while the expected Bank of England rise is supporting the pound. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3389 at 08:55 Dubai to about 1.3401 by 09:20 Dubai and EUR/USD rose in step from 1.1167 to 1.1178, which points to the dollar rather than news about the pound.

feed.title: Oil has fallen on a two-day plan to reopen Hormuz
feed.text: The banks' market has reopened with sterling little changed: GBP/USD closed Friday near 1.3389, stayed between about 1.3373 and 1.3391 in thin weekend trading, and was about 1.3385 at 07:40 Dubai on Monday. Brent fell about $2 to about $111 (about £83) in early Asian trade after Iran's foreign minister said Qatari mediators had agreed a plan with Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days, if the US meets a list of demands; Washington has not responded publicly. Cheaper oil tends to soften the dollar, but FXStreet says the chance of a December Fed rise, about 75%, is still supporting it, and at least ten shipping incidents have been reported in the region since 31 October. No report read names a cause for sterling's small moves overnight.

feed.title: Sterling has given back part of today's gain as the dollar recovered
feed.text: US employment costs rose 0.8% in the third quarter, exactly as forecast, so that figure gave little reason to move. GBP/USD still fell from 1.3429 at 16:25 Dubai to about 1.3378 at 18:00 Dubai, and EUR/USD fell in step from 1.1188 to 1.1144, which points to a firmer dollar rather than news about the pound. No report read so far names the cause of the slide, which began before the Fed's Tom Barkin spoke at 17:30 Dubai; later, at about 20:30 Dubai, the Fed's Alberto Musalem said rates will need to rise again soon, which tends to support the dollar. GBP/USD was about 1.3390 at 21:30 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has climbed as US tech shares fell and traders trimmed dollar positions
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3392 at 10:00 Dubai to about 1.3432 at 15:00 Dubai on Friday. Amazon and Intel disappointed investors, Nasdaq futures fell about 2%, and buying of US Treasuries pulled yields lower, which weakened the dollar; ING also pointed to traders reducing dollar positions before Tuesday's midterm elections. ING described the move as led by the dollar, since there was no UK data, and swaps markets were pricing a Bank of England rise on 5 November as fully expected, which gives the pound support.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened despite strong US growth figures
feed.text: On Thursday US growth came in at 3.4% against 3.2% forecast, core inflation (PCE) rose 0.3% in September as expected, and jobless claims were 194,000 against 198,000 forecast. Figures like these usually firm up a Fed rise and lift the dollar, yet the odds of a December rise fell from about 84% to about 70%, according to FXStreet, as traders trimmed their bets. GBP/USD rose from 1.3326 to 1.3335 within ten minutes, slipped to 1.3313 by 17:00 Dubai, then climbed from 1.3332 at 18:15 Dubai to 1.3375 by 19:20 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has held steady overnight as oil eased on talk of Iran diplomacy
feed.text: Brent slipped to $114.10 (about £85.70) at 07:48 Dubai, down from a close of $115.32 (about £86.60) on Wednesday, after the Wall Street Journal reported that Vice President JD Vance had written to Iran's National Security Council chief to revive peace talks, though President Trump said he had not directed the letter. Cheaper oil tends to soften the dollar, but FXStreet read Chair Warsh's tone on Wednesday as firmly hawkish, which supports it, and the two roughly cancelled out. GBP/USD stayed between 1.3301 and 1.3335 through the night and was about 1.3311 at 12:39 Dubai, against 1.3321 at the last update.
